items.title: How a Self-Described ‘Junkie’ Rode Synthetic Drugs to Oblivion — and Fame
items.summary: An Estonian addict could barely keep pace with the new drugs flooding the market. His terrifying accounts of the cruel toll they took on his body held his country in its grip.

items.title: Trump and His Aides Helped Bolsonaro Flee Brazil and Enter U.S.
items.summary: President Trump ensured Flávio Bolsonaro, who lost a presidential election in Brazil and faces multiple criminal investigations there, could enter the United States, U.S. officials said.

items.title: With No Clear Winner, How Could Israel Get a Prime Minister?
items.summary: Deadlock is possible, as neither the bloc of Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu nor his main challenger have won a majority. But there are still paths to a new government.

items.title: U.S. Hits Rwanda With New Sanctions Over a Conflict Trump Declared ‘Ended’
items.summary: The Treasury Department accused Rwanda of undermining a U.S.-brokered peace agreement by supporting a rebel group in the eastern Democratic Republic of Congo.

items.title: Suspect in France Shootings Said He Targeted Muslims and Africans, Prosecutor Says
items.summary: The suspect, identified only as Kévin T., admitted to planning the attacks near Paris last week, the prosecutor said. One person was killed and seven wounded.

items.title: Haiti Postpones Elections as Gang Violence Runs Rampant
items.summary: Haiti is in the throes of debilitating gang violence, which has kept officials from organizing an election to pick a new president.

items.title: China Is Not Happy About Fan-made A.I. Videos of Sun Wukong and Lin Daiyu
items.summary: Mash-up videos of beloved characters from Chinese classics — some made with A.I. — have caught the attention of the authorities.

items.title: In Marseille, Macron Confronts a Potent Mix of France’s Problems
items.summary: France’s second city, five years into a presidential development plan, is grappling with the social strains that have fueled protests across the country.

items.title: After Crash, Spain Asks if Its Train System Is Too Old and Prone to Human Error

items.title: China Confirms Expulsion of 33 Officials, as Xi’s Purge Deepens
items.summary: Xi Jinping has enforced loyalty as he prepares to claim a fourth term as leader. Among those removed was a prominent former diplomat, Liu Jianchao.

items.title: How One Country Became the Unlikely Crossroads of the Global A.I. Boom

items.title: In China, the War on Mosquitoes Has Entered the A.I. Era

items.title: Inflation Accelerated in October, PCE Index Shows

items.title: U.S. GDP Increased 3.4% in Third Quarter
items.summary: The economy grew 3.4 percent in the third quarter, the fastest pace in a year. Strong spending and growth contrast with the poor marks many voters are giving the economy.

items.summary: Investors are showing little patience for lavish spending and meager returns on companies’ artificial intelligence bets.

items.summary: A Chinese start-up has developed a device that uses artificial intelligence and lasers to kill mosquitoes. But there are safety concerns for people and other creatures nearby when the device is in action.

items.title: Bodacious A.I. Bots Are Stealing Jokes From Young Female Comedians
items.summary: Swiping jokes word for word, these bodacious bots mainly lift from young female comedians. What’s so insidious is how they’re subtly changing us, the audience.

items.title: Alphabet’s Revenue Rises 25% as Profit Falls
items.summary: The company has been spending relentlessly to build A.I. and said it would increase those investments next year. Profit dropped because of changes to the value of its investments.
